parakeet: Colonial blood trails. Blood theology didn't stay in the pews. It marched with conquistadors, it rolled with missionaries, it blessed genocide in Jesus' name. The logic was simple. If blood is the price of salvation, then the shedding of it, yours or someone else's, must be holy. And that logic justified slavery, colonialism, and conversion by force, because if Christ's blood saves, then saving others meant spilling more. That's why entire continents were baptized in violence. Why indigenous people were told their culture had to die, why black bodies were chained beneath crosses, why prisons today still echo with sermons about sin and discipline. This wasn't the gospel. It was a theology of conquest dressed up as divine order. You don't get global domination out of compassion. You get it by canonizing sacrifice and calling it righteousness. This isn't ancient history. It's inherited trauma, still alive, still shaping policy, still quoted on pulpits and senate floors, concerts and classrooms alike.
